content:
Earlier this year, after the Liquid Glass design first launched on iOS, WhatsApp is now working to extend this design to more interface elements. Here are the details.

Liquid Glass is coming to the WhatsApp drawing editor and video player

If this sounds familiar, we apologize: WhatsApp is planning to extend the Liquid Glass redesign to more parts of the app.

Earlier this year, after more than six months of testing, WhatsApp finally rolled out the first wave of Liquid Glass updates more broadly.

At the time, the company was also working to apply the new design to elements such as the voice message player, message reactions, and contextual menus, but these changes have remained limited to the beta version of the app.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, the latest iOS beta of WhatsApp shows that the company is preparing to bring Liquid Glass's visual style to more interface elements—namely the drawing editor and the video player progress bar.

From WABetaInfo:

It's worth noting that some 9to5Mac readers have often said that their iPhones have still not received the first wave of Liquid Glass updates; however, today's news shows that Meta continues to adopt this new visual language, not only on iOS, but also on macOS and iPadOS.

Back to today's news, WABetaInfo points out: "This feature is still under development and has not yet been made available to beta testers."
